title: Annex A · Formula Reference
text: The core equations behind every model in this course, using the η/ξ notation introduced in Lecture 01.

title: Annex A · Formula Reference
text:
Measurement model
Each indicator loads on a single latent factor plus unique error.
\[ y_i = \lambda_i \eta + \varepsilon_i \]

title: Annex A · Formula Reference
text:
Structural path
A latent factor predicting another, as fit in Lecture 04.
\[ \eta_2 = \beta \eta_1 + \zeta \]

title: Annex A · Formula Reference
text:
Fit indices
χ² is the model chi-square, df its degrees of freedom, N the sample size, relative to the baseline model b.
\[ \text{RMSEA} = \sqrt{\max\!\left(\frac{\chi^2 - df}{df\,(N-1)},\ 0\right)} \]
\[ \text{CFI} = 1 - \frac{\max(\chi^2_m - df_m,\ 0)}{\max(\chi^2_b - df_b,\ 0)} \]






Note



SRMR is the root mean square of standardized residual covariances — reported directly by lavaan/Mplus, rarely computed by hand.

title: 04 · Structural Equation Models
text:
Fitting in R (lavaan)

sem_model <- '
  eta1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4
  eta2 =~ y5 + y6 + y7 + y8
  eta2 ~ eta1
  outcome ~ eta2
'
fit <- sem(sem_model, data = lvm_data)







Warning



A well-fitting measurement model does not guarantee the structural paths are identified or correctly directed — check theory first.

title: 01 · Introduction to Latent Variables
text:
A latent variable is a construct that is not directly observed but is inferred from a set of measured indicators. IQ, socioeconomic status, and depression severity are all latent — we never measure them directly, only their manifestations.






Note



Throughout this course, indicators are denoted y and latent factors η (eta) or ξ (xi), following Mplus/LISREL convention.

title: 01 · Introduction to Latent Variables
text:
The three model families
This course covers three related model families, in increasing order of assumption strength: exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and full structural equation models (SEM) that relate latent factors to one another.

title: Annex C · Annotated Output
text:
IRT · Rasch (1PL)
Discrimination is fixed at 1 for every item — only difficulty (location) varies.

        a      b       g
item_01 1.000  -0.842  0
item_02 1.000  0.315   0
item_03 1.000  1.204   0

M2(df) = 18.4(20), p = .560

a is fixed to 1 across items — that constraint is what makes it a Rasch model, not a 2PL.
b is difficulty on the θ scale; a negative b means low-ability respondents still answer correctly.
A non-significant M2 (p > .05) means the model is not rejected.

title: Annex C · Annotated Output
text:
IRT · Partial Credit Model
Ordered polytomous items — one threshold per step between categories, discrimination still fixed at 1.

          b1      b2      b3
item_01  -1.20   -0.05    0.98
item_02  -0.88    0.12    1.15
item_03  -0.60    0.71    0.55

Step thresholds (Andrich thresholds) increase monotonically — steps get harder as expected.
item_03’s b2 > b3: a threshold reversal — common with sparse categories, doesn’t itself mean disordered categories.

title: Annex C · Annotated Output
text:
IRT · Graded Response Model
A 2PL for ordered categories — discrimination now varies by item, thresholds model cumulative logits.

        a       b1      b2      b3
item_01 1.84    -1.10   -0.02   1.05
item_02 0.97    -0.75    0.30   1.40
item_03 2.21    -0.90   -0.10   0.88

a varies by item — item_01 discriminates more sharply between adjacent ability levels than item_02.
b1 < b2 < b3 within every item — GRM thresholds must stay ordered, unlike the PCM’s per-category steps.

title: Annex C · Annotated Output
text:
Multilevel model
Students nested in schools — a random intercept partitions variance into within- and between-school components.

Random effects:
 Groups   Name        Variance
 school   (Intercept) 4.82
 Residual             15.31

ICC = 0.240

Between-school variance in the intercept — how much average outcomes differ across schools.
Residual (within-school, between-student) variance.
ICC = 4.82 / (4.82 + 15.31) — 24% of total variance sits between schools, well above the ~5% threshold where ignoring nesting would matter.
